issue.title: Find the test that leaves a stale lock in the real checkout
issue.description: Proposed by sase-1rq.2.1.4.1.3 note #8. Monitor aa3fzgn042n3 on 4a7ce0f330 left a zero-byte .git/index.lock at 2026-11-07 19:50:03 EST (+2821.7s), no holder afterwards; it had to be removed before host finalization. Likely an index-refreshing git command killed mid-write, but root cause is not proven. In-flight candidates: tests/llm_provider/test_commit_finalizer_auto_sdd_status.py, tests/test_commit_type_tag_contract.py, tests/test_commit_workflow_bead_lifecycle_e2e.py, tests/doctor/test_checks_project.py, tests/test_bead/test_task_beads.py, tests/test_linked_repo_materialization.py. Extend tests/_checkout_leak_guard.py to identify newly created .git/*.lock per test without touching pre-existing/foreign locks, reproduce with restricted candidates and their shard order, then isolate test Git work in temp repos. Do not add blanket lock deletion. Large size because causal test and mechanism require investigation. All-status searches, last-week sweep, and active epic review found no matching lock-creation issue; this is not the bounded production lock-probe timeout.

task_type_fields.impact: Leaves the workspace unable to write the Git index or complete host commits until safely recovered.
task_type_fields.repro: Relayed observed incident: aa3fzgn042n3 full 26-worker/two-CPU repeat on 4a7ce0f330, lock first seen +2821.7s. Use recorded in-flight candidates and per-test Git-lock guard to attribute the writer; not yet deterministic.

issue.creation_reason: A completed contention repeat left an unowned index lock that blocked host commits. The responsible test is unknown and the existing checkout leak guard does not cover Git lock files.
